answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to complete a proof of useful work bound to its own key, so one solved task cannot be copied across a thousand shells. Like a relic whose origin can be checked, each proof is verified against real output and then expires, forcing a new cedar of fakes to pay full cost again from its nadir. With rewards capped per identity, multiplying accounts multiplies cost without multiplying payout, so forgery stops paying.
